summary: Root cause identified (high confidence, ~0.80): the mTLS client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal used by payment-service for outbound calls to bank-partner-api expired at 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z, so every transfer submission to the bank fails the TLS handshake from that instant and ~97-98% of payments never complete. The failures are parked in PENDING_RETRY instead of surfacing as synchronous HTTP 5xx, which is why the human-facing error_rate panel stayed green (mean 0.21%) while bank_api_error_rate sat at exactly 100% for all 105 buckets and payment_success_rate collapsed to ~2.5%. Two lesser hypotheses (bank-partner-api partner-side TLS/trust change, and the 11:20Z bank.api.timeout_ms config bump) are unsupported: the untruncated alert-45 chain names only our own client cert as the expired leaf, with no partner server/intermediate CN, and the observed error class is certificate expiry rather than timeout. Same-class precedent HIST-106 (settlement-service client cert expired, no renewal automation) supports this failure mode.

ranked_hypotheses.title: payment-service mTLS client certificate expired at 12:15Z, breaking the bank-partner-api edge
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal used by payment-service for mTLS to bank-partner-api expired at 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z (notAfter). From that instant every outbound call to bank-partner-api fails the TLS handshake, so ~100% of transfers cannot be submitted to the bank. The failures are parked in state PENDING_RETRY rather than surfaced as synchronous HTTP 5xx, so the aggregate HTTP error_rate panel stays green while bank_api_error_rate goes to 100% and payment_success_rate collapses.

causal_chain.claim: payment-service holds a client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal whose notAfter is exactly 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z; no renewal automation ran (HIST-106 is the same failure mode on sibling settlement-service, 'no renewal automation').

At/after 12:15:00Z every mTLS handshake from payment-service to bank-partner-api is rejected; first ERROR 12:15:27Z, 140 'mTLS handshake rejected' entries plus 171 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)' entries.

The full untruncated alert-45 chain (7 ERRORs, 12:16:44Z-12:20:31Z) names OUR client certificate as the expired leaf in every entry: 'our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z'; no bank-partner-api server or intermediate cert CN appears in any alert-45 payload.
The earliest signature is caller-side rejection: 7 untruncated 'payment <n> marked PENDING_RETRY: mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected' entries, first 12:15:27Z, last 12:18:19Z.
bank-partner-api calls fail at 100% for the entire window (bank_api_error_rate = 100.0% on 105/105 buckets 12:15-13:55Z).
Payments cannot complete: payment_success_rate collapses to ~2.48% mean (1.44-3.5%).

Failed transfers are parked in PENDING_RETRY instead of surfacing as synchronous HTTP 5xx, and request_rate stays flat ~100 req/s with no retry storm, so the aggregate error_rate (0.21% mean) and latency_p99 stay flat and the human-facing panel stays green.
Support sees ~40 tickets about failed fund transfers in a 15-minute window; failure path is the external callee edge payment-service -> bank-partner-api.

assumptions: The notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z timestamp in the error text is the local client certificate's expiry (explicitly labelled 'our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal'), i.e. caller-side, not a partner-side cert.
The bank partner did not itself initiate a TLS trust/anchor change at the same instant (partner has no telemetry, cannot be observed directly).
PENDING_RETRY failures are not counted in the aggregate error_rate by design.
The runtime-log notAfter equals the inventory-recorded expiry (no cert-inventory surface was available to corroborate).

ranked_hypotheses.title: bank-partner-api (external vendor) degraded or changed its mTLS/TLS trust configuration at 12:15Z
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The third-party bank connector began rejecting payment-service's handshakes at onset — either the partner rotated its server certificate / trust anchor or changed cipher/client-CA requirements. From payment-service's side this presents as mTLS handshake rejection and alert 45, indistinguishable from a local cert problem because the partner has no telemetry.

causal_chain.claim: The failing path is the external callee edge payment-service -> bank-partner-api, kind external, has_telemetry=false.
Handshakes to the partner are rejected beginning 12:15:00-12:15:27Z, producing mTLS-rejection and expired-certificate ERROR entries.
100% of bank API calls fail, collapsing payment_success_rate to ~2.5%.
Historical precedent HIST-105 (2025-11-19) shows payment failures caused by a bank partner returning 5xx for 40 min, category dependency_failure, same symptom shape via the same edge.
Because the partner has no logs/metrics, a partner-side fault cannot be excluded from internal telemetry alone and no rotation/advisory record is exposed for the vendor edge.

assumptions: A partner-side server-cert/trust-anchor failure could produce caller-side 'expired certificate (alert 45)' text naming our client cert as the expired leaf, and the T+0 coincidence with our notAfter instant would be accidental.

ranked_hypotheses.title: 11:20Z 'bank.api.timeout_ms' 3000->5000 config change silently converted hard failures into parked PENDING_RETRY payments
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Raising the bank API timeout from 3s to 5s at 11:20Z by p.nair changed failure semantics on the bank edge, causing transfers to be parked in PENDING_RETRY and thus invisible to the aggregate error_rate panel. The change is the only config change in the window and predates onset.

causal_chain.claim: Exactly one config change exists in 10:00-13:59Z: payment-service bank.api.timeout_ms 3000 -> 5000 at 11:20:00Z.
The longer timeout pushes slow/failed bank calls into an async retry path instead of surfacing them synchronously, so error_rate stays flat.
Resulting parkings/retries manifest as customer-visible transfer failures.

assumptions: A timeout raise can cause mTLS handshake rejection errors with alert 45 'expired certificate' — no mechanism supports this.
A ~55-minute quiet gap between the change and onset is causal rather than incidental.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The observed error class is TLS certificate expiry (alert 45) with the expired leaf named as our client cert (F23, F24, F27), not a timeout/deadline exhaustion; latency_p99 and request_rate stay flat with no retry storm (F8, F10). The change precedes onset by ~55 min across a quiet gap, and bank_api_error_rate is exactly 100% of calls — impossible for a timeout-tuning effect. Only candidate-change proximity supports it.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared datastore/queue (ledger-db or kafka) saturating, stalling payment completion
ranked_hypotheses.statement: ledger-db (shared by order-, portfolio-, payment- and settlement-service) or the shared kafka broker degraded at onset, stalling payment completion while payment-service's own HTTP error rate stayed green. Precedent HIST-114 (ledger-db disk full from retained WAL) shows this class of failure on this component.

causal_chain.claim: ledger-db and kafka are shared=true; ledger-db has four upstream dependents including payment-service.
A shared store/queue stall would slow or fail payment persistence, parking transfers.
Only payment-service is shown failing; its failure is specifically on the bank edge, not the db/queue edge.

assumptions: No telemetry for ledger-db/kafka was retrieved, so degradation cannot be positively excluded.
Order/portfolio/settlement dependents would also be impacted but were not checked.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The error signature is a TLS/certificate failure on the bank-partner-api external edge (F7, F9, F15, F23), not a DB/queue error. bank_api_error_rate sits at exactly 100% for the whole window while latency_p99 and request_rate stay flat — inconsistent with a store/queue stall, which would elevate latency and affect the other ledger-db dependents equally (F16 shows they are not implicated).

facts.statement: payment-service error logs begin at 2026-04-02T12:15:27Z with 'mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected' (140 occurrences) and a paired 'bank-partner-api call failed: remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45); our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z' (171 occurrences, first at 12:16:44Z).

The untruncated alert-45 chain for 12:15:00-12:21:00Z contains exactly 7 ERROR entries (first 12:16:44Z, last 12:20:31Z) and every one names OUR client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z as the expired leaf; no bank-partner-api server or intermediate cert CN appears in any alert-45 payload.

The paired mTLS-rejection entries (7, untruncated) are all the same leaf-side failure on the caller's own cert: 'payment <n> marked PENDING_RETRY: mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected', first 12:15:27Z, last 12:18:19Z, all ERROR.
bank_api_error_rate was 100.0% at every bucket from 12:15:00Z through 13:55:00Z (105/105 points, min=max=100) and payment_success_rate collapsed to ~2.48% mean (range 1.44-3.5%).

The reported service's aggregate error_rate stayed normal across the whole window (mean 0.21%, max 0.32%, 105/105 points) and latency_p99_ms stayed flat (mean 139.77 ms, max 157.41 ms), confirming the green panel did not reflect the transfer failures.

payment-service request_rate stayed flat at ~100 req/s (mean 100.52) with no retry storm or traffic surge, and affected payments were parked in state 'PENDING_RETRY' rather than surfacing as synchronous HTTP 5xx — consistent with the aggregate error_rate staying green.

The failure sits on payment-service's external callee edge to bank-partner-api (kind external, has_telemetry=false); ledger-db (kind db) and kafka (queue-produce) are also direct callees, so the failure point is the external bank edge, not payment-service's datastore/queue.
bank-partner-api is an external dependency with no logs/metrics of its own and can only be observed through its caller payment-service.

ledger-db is shared=true with four upstream dependents (order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service, settlement-service), but only payment-service's bank-edge failure is implicated; the other callers are not shown failing.

No deployments were recorded across ALL services in the incident window (none in 11:00-13:59Z); the only deployment near the incident is settlement-service v1.9.0 at 2026-04-02T10:30:00Z (status live, not rolled back). No deployment coincides with onset.

recommended_actions.action: Immediate mitigation: renew/replace the expired mTLS client certificate for payment-service (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal) and deploy the renewed cert/secret to the payment-service bank-partner-api client, then restart/reload the affected pods so new handshakes use the valid cert.

Reissuing this specific credential is the only change that stops the failures.

what_would_change_the_conclusion: An alert-45 or TLS-handshake payload naming a bank-partner-api server or intermediate certificate CN as the expired/rejected leaf (rather than our CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal) would point to a partner-side certificate problem and overturn H1.

Successful mTLS handshakes to bank-partner-api resuming immediately upon renewal of our client cert (with no partner-side change) would confirm H1; conversely, continued handshake failures after renewing our cert would show a partner-side cause.

Evidence that payment-service's last successful bank-partner-api call was well before 12:15Z (an earlier onset), or an independent cert-inventory record showing a different notAfter than 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z, would shift the timing/attribution.

Evidence of simultaneous degradation of the other ledger-db dependents (order-service, portfolio-service, settlement-service) or of elevated latency/DB-pool/cpu signals would revive H4 (shared datastore/queue saturation) as a contributing cause.

Evidence that the 11:20Z 'bank.api.timeout_ms' 3000->5000 change altered failure-parking semantics such that timeout/deadline errors are being misexpressed as alert-45 cert expiry would revive H3; the observed error class (certificate expiry, latency flat) currently argues strongly against this.
